dropping the patch based on review feedback

THis isn't really true.  The intent of the policy was one file per piece of hardware.

There might be cases where a piece of hardware "acts" differently dependent on location, or if it's in different modes.   Those different "modes" are intended to be captured in the array, so we keep one file per config.

Lets make sure the PR matches what the policy intent is.

> THis isn't really true. The intent of the policy was one file per piece of hardware.

I should have probably read the ```README.md``` where this policy is mentioned 👍

I am wondering if the policy intent is worth keeping.

In case of a complicated piece of hardware with variants and modes requiring different configuration files, i would rather have a folder to keep them in.

This can give the advantage to easily ```diff``` the variants of that piece of hardware.

With a combined file, it would still be possible to ```diff``` them but may require special scripts. I am wondering how you handle this use-case.

I see the concern that people may lose track of multiple configurations supporting a piece of hardware if they are not properly kept in folders. But i would assume good intent from people to keep their configurations organized.

There is another patch in this change to introduce ```CompatibleHardware``` property at EM Config toplevel to support another feature. Maybe that can help to keep track of multiple configurations supporting a piece of hardware.

> > THis isn't really true. The intent of the policy was one file per piece of hardware.
> 
> I should have probably read the ```README.md``` where this policy is mentioned 👍
> 

As the guy that wrote the readme.... I highly recommend reading it 😊

> I am wondering if the policy intent is worth keeping.
> 
> In case of a complicated piece of hardware with variants and modes requiring different configuration files, i would rather have a folder to keep them in.

I disagree.  I would rather we use folders to indicate classes and manufacturers of hardware.  The goal with the "one file per hardware" is that new hardware could be added using a single include.  I don't really want to lose that ability.

> 
> This can give the advantage to easily ```diff``` the variants of that piece of hardware.
> 
> With a combined file, it would still be possible to ```diff``` them but may require special scripts. I am wondering how you handle this use-case.

The script seems like it would be a line or two of python.  If we're worried about that case, we can check that into a scripts repo, but I don't think the general "diff these two identical hardware configs" is a common use case.  

> 
> I see the concern that people may lose track of multiple configurations supporting a piece of hardware if they are not properly kept in folders. But i would assume good intent from people to keep their configurations organized.

It's much easier to just be able to enforce it as convention.  While we may assume good intent, a lot of people don't read the docs on intent (see above 😊) so the more clear we can make it without needing documentation, the better.  Certainly appending _N to the end of the filename is more subtle as a convention than what we have.

> 
> There is another patch in this change to introduce ```CompatibleHardware``` property at EM Config toplevel to support another feature. Maybe that can help to keep track of multiple configurations supporting a piece of hardware.

Already left comments on that as well.  I think that's just a way to drive community factions rather than community consensus.  we can discuss more in that patch.

> I disagree. I would rather we use folders to indicate classes and manufacturers of hardware. The goal with the "one file per hardware" is that new hardware could be added using a single include. I don't really want to lose that ability.

I had a solution with regex to select based on folders. Which you did not agree with.

> The goal with the "one file per hardware" is that new hardware could be added using a single include. I don't really want to lose that ability.

Why is that important to have that capability? It's not like there is any guarantees provided by having it be in one file?


If you have a single piece of hardware, why would it even result in multiple EM configs. It should be configuration of a specific 'Type', right? Like 'Powersupply' or 'Board'.

What is the advantage of splitting this config into multiple files.  The reasoning on next line is more around cosmetic stuff. TBH One can also prefer to keep the related conifguration in a single file to avoid creating multiple files.
Has there been any formal discussion on this change?

Thanks for taking an interest in this change 😊

> TBH One can also prefer to keep the related configuration in a single file to avoid creating multiple files.

To EM, these configurations are unrelated. I do not think there is any code which would treat them differently based on which file they come from.
If you have a concern around losing track of related configuration, i think creating a folder for related configuration files can solve that issue.

> What is the advantage of splitting this config into multiple files

I want to simplify this aspect of EM which will
- simplify the schema
- simplify runtime code
- simplify scripts for validation of configuration
- indentation is reduced 
- no '2 ways of doing something'

> Has there been any formal discussion on this change?

Not much discussion. I think the patch is the right place to discuss this.

If you want to progress this forward, I'd recommend some stages:

1. For files that have an array with a single element, that's obviously incorrect, migrate those in a patchset.
2. For the remaining configs, have your script walk through and ensure that the probe statements are very similar, and differ only by a location parameter.  If they don't split the files.  Do this in patchset 2.

This file for example is already correct.  This riser might take a different name dependent on where it's detected.

Please make sure your PR accounts for "correct" usages.

Yes, I agree, there are a lot of incorrect usages present, we should clean those up, but I don't think we can do that with a general purpose script.
This is a counter example that SHOULD Be split up.  Clearly these are distinct model numbers and separate boards.  They should have their own files.
Having 30 independent files for this really seems complex.  Generally we would use the % replace expressions to collapse this into a single file.
This is another example use.  These power supplies have 2 node id gpios that determine their "index" and makes them show up in different locations.
